_: Root specification for the engine-coverage denominator (see engine-scope.sh).
Every entry names symbols in the pinned instrumented build
a place control enters KiCad from outside; everything transitively reachable from
the `work` roots is the engine, everything else is out of scope BY CONSTRUCTION.
`regex`/`exact` match the mangled symbol name with any object-file namespace

why: kicad/kicad_cli.cpp. Process entry. Reaches PGM_KICAD startup, argparse, the
COMMAND_ENTRY table walk and COMMAND::Perform. NOTE the `main` node is shared
with thirdparty/lemon/lemon.c, which gcovr excludes from the report anyway.
CLI::<X>_COMMAND::doPerform(KIWAY&) -- the 30 kicad-cli subcommands plus the
CLI::COMMAND base. These have to be roots rather than fall out of `main`,
because the COMMAND objects are file-scope statics (kicad/kicad_cli.cpp:124-176)
whose only constructor call is in _GLOBAL__sub_I_, and main dispatches through
COMMAND::Perform -> virtual doPerform. `per_symbol` gives one closure per
subcommand so a gap can be attributed to the verb that would reach it.
kicad-cli dlopen()s _pcbnew/_eeschema/_cvpcb.kiface and calls into them through
the KIFACE vtable (common/kiway.cpp). A static reference graph cannot cross a
dlopen boundary or an indirect vtable call, so these are explicit roots.
Rule: root every KIFACE virtual (include/kiway.h:155) whose signature is free
of GUI types -- excludes CreateKiWindow, HandleJobConfig and GetActions.
SaveFileAs/ProjectChanged/CancelPreload/PreloadLibraries are rooted even where
no CLI path is known to call them: rooting can only widen the denominator,
the safe direction for a coverage figure.
Static initialisers of every object in the build. They genuinely execute on
every kicad-cli invocation, which trivially inflates coverage -- but they are
also load-bearing (KiCad registers DRC test providers, IO plugins and settings
schemas from file-scope statics), so excluding them would MISS real engine
code. Kept, and reported SEPARATELY from work-reachable lines.

gui.excluded.CreateKiWindow.why: Returns a wxWindow*. The whole editor-frame/tool/dialog tree hangs off it.

gui.excluded.HandleJobConfig.why: Takes a wxWindow* parent; its only caller is kicad/dialogs/panel_jobset.cpp.

why: The signature rule, applied to every function, not just the KIFACE vtable: a
function taking/returning a top-level wxWidgets GUI type or a wxWidgets event
cannot be called by kicad-cli. Matched on the Itanium-mangled name (exact token,
not substring). `[0-9]wx[A-Za-z]*Event` covers the whole wxEvent family.
`8wxWindow` is DELIBERATELY ABSENT: a wxWindow* parameter is very often an
optional parent, not proof of GUI-ness (e.g. ZONE_FILLER_TOOL::FillAllZones
takes one but the CLI passes nullptr) -- excluding it dropped real DRC/refill
code from scope. wxDialog/wxFrame/wxTopLevelWindow don't have that escape
hatch. Needed because RTA seeds off constructors: a file-scope static whose
vtable contains window-taking methods re-imports the GUI through the back door.
Validated: adding this barrier must not increase the executed-but-out-of-scope
count (`engine_validate.py negative`), or it cut something the suite runs.
TOOL_INTERACTIVE::setTransitions() is where each interactive tool binds its
TOOL_EVENT handlers. A CLI run has no event loop, so no transition is ever
taken -- but every tool's constructor calls it, making it the single RTA hub
that pulled the whole editor tool set into scope. Does NOT exclude tool code
the CLI genuinely uses: ZONE_FILLER_TOOL is still reachable via the DRC/refill
path with this barrier in place.

deferred_cut.^_ZN3CLI21PCB_EXPORT_3D_COMMAND9doPerfor: 3D/STEP/GLB/VRML export CLI verb -- deferred, not in the committed suite
deferred_cut.^_ZN3CLI18PCB_IMPORT_COMMAND9doPerformER: third-party board import verb -- not covered by the suite
deferred_cut.^_ZN19PCBNEW_JOBS_HANDLER13JobExportStep: the kiface side of `pcb export step/glb/vrml`
_deferred_cut_note: These are BARRIERS, not roots. The closure is computed twice -- once normally,
once with these nodes never entered -- and the difference is the code that only
a deferred CLI path can reach. A per-verb closure cannot answer this, because
IFACE::HandleJob dispatches on job type and so reaches every job handler from
the single kiface root; cutting the entry point is the only separable question.
Both halves of each verb have to be cut: the kicad-cli-side doPerform AND the
kiface-side handler, because the two are in different binaries and the handler
is reachable from the jobs-handler constructor, not from doPerform.
